facts.claim: Britannica describes Lohengrin as an opera by Richard Wagner, first performed on 28 August 1850 at Weimar, given by Franz Liszt.

Britannica describes The Four Seasons (Le quattro stagioni) as a group of four violin concerti by Antonio Vivaldi, written about 1720 and published in 1725 (Amsterdam) within Il cimento dell'armonia e dell'inventione; Spring is Concerto No. 1 in E major, in three movements (Allegro, Largo e pianissimo sempre, Allegro).
Britannica describes Clair de lune as the third movement of Suite bergamasque, a four-movement piano suite by Claude Debussy, begun in 1890 and revised and published in 1905.

IMSLP lists Franz Schubert's Ave Maria (alternative title Ellens Gesang III / Hymne an die Jungfrau), D.839, Op.52 No.6, for voice and piano, composed April 1825 and first published 1826; text is Adam Storck's German translation after Walter Scott's The Lady of the Lake (1810).
IMSLP lists Edward Elgar's Salut d'amour (Love's Greeting; Liebesgruss), Op.12, for violin and piano, composed 1888, first published 1889 (London: Schott), dedicated to Caroline Alice Elgar.
